samples.summary: The rewritten undo-floor check fails OPEN: any failure to locate the floor entry by identity permits undoing past the initial document load
samples.evidence:
`canUndo()` now resolves the initial-load boundary by reference: `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2977), with `undoFloorMark` captured as a live entry reference in `markUndoFloor()` (line 860). When the mark is not found `lastIndexOf` returns `-1`, which is `< stack.length - 1` for any non-empty stack, so the guard answers "undoable". That is the documented intent for the cap-eviction case, but it makes the guard fail open for *every* reason the identity can fail to match, not just eviction. The whole point of the floor (see the comment at line 616 and `docs/tasks/archive/2026/05/20260505-undo-destroys-initial-block-todo.md`) is that undoing past the load write destroys the blocks the cursor and every collaborator reference, and the reverse of `writeFullDocument` is synced to all peers — so a fail-open here is document-wide content destruction rather than a UI annoyance.

The identity now depends on an unspecified, test-named SDK accessor returning the *live* stack array with entry references preserved (`this.doc.getUndoStackForTest()`, used in production at lines 859 and 2973). I could not confirm that contract: no `@yorkie-js` package is present in this checkout (`node_modules` is not installed), so I could not read the SDK implementation. If any SDK version returns a mapped/copied stack (entirely plausible for an accessor whose name marks it as test-only), the mark never matches, the floor silently disappears for every session, and one extra Cmd+Z past the user's own edits wipes the loaded document. The previous depth comparison degraded in the safe direction (it refused undos); this one grants them. A cheap hardening is to keep a depth alongside the mark and require *both* (e.g. treat "mark absent" as allowed only when the stack has demonstrably shrunk from the bottom), or to assert once at load that the freshly captured mark is findable in a subsequent read.

samples.summary: The async-resumed clipboard write re-validates lifecycle state but not write permission, and `readOnly` is never re-armed for a mounted editor
samples.evidence: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard()` resumes after `await navigator.clipboard.readText()` and now re-checks two invariants — `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4254) — with the diff's own comment noting the read can take arbitrarily long because a permission prompt is a user interaction. The one invariant it does not re-check is whether this session may still write. That would be moot if `readOnly` could not change, but it is captured once at construction (`TextEditor` ctor arg, text-editor.ts:717-719) and the mount effect that builds the store and calls `initialize(container, store, theme, readOnly)` (docs-view.tsx:359) has dependency list `[didMount, doc]` (docs-view.tsx:573) — `readOnly` is absent. So a share-link role that resolves to `viewer` on a refetch (`const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:322) flips the surrounding UI to view-only while the mounted editor keeps its stale writable flag and every `readOnly` guard inside `TextEditor` keeps answering false. Attack shape: a user with edit access starts a Cmd+Shift+V (or simply keeps the tab open) while the owner revokes edit access; the resumed write, and every subsequent keystroke, still reaches `YorkieDocStore` and syncs to all peers. This matters more than a typical client-side flag because `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42` records that the server-side Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), i.e. the client flag *is* the write boundary in the default configuration. I could not confirm that the share-link resolution actually refetches within a mount, so confidence is low; the defect is pre-existing rather than introduced here, but the diff is precisely the change that decides which invariants an async-resumed write revalidates, which is why I raise it on this guard.

Glob **/node_modules/**/yorkie-js-sdk/**/*.d.ts (no files — deps not installed)
Grep history\.(undo|redo)\(\) in packages/frontend/src to enumerate bypasses of the canUndo gate
Read yorkie-doc-store.ts:2951-2982 (undo/redo/canUndo), 826-861 (setDocument/markUndoFloor)

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: canUndo() at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2977 returns `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1`, which is true when the mark is absent (-1), and markUndoFloor() at lines 858-861 captures a live entry reference from doc.getUndoStackForTest(). So this is not a 'not-present' refutation. It is out of scope for the Security lens. The undo floor is not an authorization or access-control gate: it does not discriminate by identity, role, or ownership, and it protects the local user from their own Cmd+Z walking past the initial-load write. Any actor who can reach undo() (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2956-2961, which just forwards to doc.history.undo() with no permission check being weakened) already possesses full edit rights on that document and can achieve the same content destruction directly via block edits, select-all-delete, or setDocument() — all of which sync to peers identically. Defeating the floor therefore crosses no privilege boundary and yields no escalation, IDOR, or bypass. The finding also implicates no secret, injection sink, signature/HMAC check, randomness, SSRF, deserialization, or path handling. What remains is a guard whose degradation direction changed from conservative to permissive, resting on an unverified assumption about whether the SDK accessor returns the live array with entry references preserved — a correctness property of a UX/data-integrity guard, which this rubric explicitly defers to the correctness lens ('General logic bugs (correctness lens) ... do not report'). The reviewer's severity argument concerns blast radius of a bug, not the absence or bypassability of a security control.

verdict.reason: The finding's code reading is accurate — `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` re-checks only `disposed`/`pasting` (text-editor.ts:4254), `readOnly` is a ctor-captured field (text-editor.ts:191,717-719), no setReadOnly-style re-arm exists, and the mount effect deps are `[didMount, doc]` (docs-view.tsx:573). But the exploit chain requires `readOnly` to change while a DocsView stays mounted, and that transition is not present in this repo. `<DocsView>` has exactly two call sites: docs-detail.tsx:280-290 never passes `readOnly` (owner route always writable), and shared-document.tsx:362-368 passes `resolved.role === "viewer"` (shared-document.tsx:322). `resolved` is written by the single `setResolved(data)` at shared-document.tsx:1095 inside a one-shot `resolveShareLink(token).then(...)` keyed `[token]` (1086-1102); a repo-wide grep for `resolveShareLink|setResolved` shows no react-query wrapper, poll, refetch, invalidation or subscription that updates the role. Until `resolved` is set the component renders `<Loader/>` (1104-1106), so the role is fixed before `initialize(container, store, theme, readOnly)` (docs-view.tsx:359) runs and never changes after. The only way it changes is a new token, which also changes `docKey` (shared-document.tsx:984-993) and hence the `doc` the mount effect depends on, re-running initialize with the fresh flag — and that visitor already holds the new token, so no escalation. Additionally, when `readOnly` is true the Cmd+Shift+V entry is dead at text-editor.ts:1096-1101 before reaching line 1375. Post-revocation enforcement after attach is a server-side webhook concern (read-only.ts:38-42), not a property of this async re-validation. No reachable authorization bypass.
